title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 先声药业拿下凌科药业泽普昔替尼皮肤科独家商业化权益，国产JAK1抑制剂特应性皮炎NDA获受理 先声药业拿下凌科药业泽普昔替尼皮肤科独家商业化权益，国产JAK1抑制剂特应性皮炎NDA获受理 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 2026/11/03 2569 JAK1 凌科药业（杭州）有限公司 强直性脊柱炎 江苏先声医药科技有限公司 特应性皮炎 11月2日，先声药业发布公告，宣布与凌科药业（浙江）股份有限公司达成新一轮合作，获得选择性JAK1抑制剂泽普昔替尼在中国大陆及港澳台地区，用于成人中重度特应性皮炎及其他皮肤科适应症的独家商业化权益。图源：先声药业企业公告这是双方继2022年3月首次合作后的再次携手。此前，先声药业已获得泽普昔替尼治疗类风湿关节炎、强直性脊柱炎两大适应症的大中华区独家商业化权益。本次合作进一步将商业化布局拓展至皮肤科领域。值得关注的是，泽普昔替尼治疗中重度特应性皮炎的关键性Ⅲ期临床研究已完成，相关新药上市申请（NDA）于2026年4月获国家药监局药品审评中心（CDE）受理。一、二度合作，商业化权益再扩容泽普昔替尼由凌科药业自主研发，是一款高选择性、口服第二代JAK1抑制剂，正在开发用于类风湿关节炎、特应性皮炎及强直性脊柱炎等炎症和自身免疫性疾病。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次合作是双方2022年首次合作后的进一步扩容。先声药业在原有风湿免疫适应症商业化权益基础上，新增获得泽普昔替尼在特应性皮炎及其他皮肤科适应症的独家商业化权益。摩熵医药数据库显示，目前，JAK3抑制剂SIM-0280也在布局自身免疫性疾病领域，尚处于临床前研究阶段。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库对于先声药业而言，此次合作有望进一步丰富自身免疫领域产品组合，并利用现有商业化体系推进产品市场开发；对于凌科药业而言，则可以借助先声药业的商业化能力，为产品后续上市及市场推广提供支持。双方此次合作的具体交易金额、里程碑付款及销售分成比例尚未披露。二、III期临床完成，特应性皮炎上市申请获受理临床数据方面，泽普昔替尼治疗中重度特应性皮炎的Ⅲ期研究共纳入356例患者。结果显示，治疗第16周时，两个剂量组在EASI-75、vIGA-AD 0/1及瘙痒改善等终点上均显著优于安慰剂组。起效时间方面，给药后第1天即可观察到瘙痒改善，第2周开始出现皮损改善。安全性方面，不良事件以轻中度为主，严重不良事件和特别关注不良事件发生率与安慰剂组基本相当，未发现新的安全性信号。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除特应性皮炎外，泽普昔替尼治疗类风湿关节炎的Ⅲ期临床研究已完成，针对强直性脊柱炎的Ⅲ期临床开发项目仍在进行中。目前，特应性皮炎领域已有度普利尤单抗等生物制剂，以及乌帕替尼、阿布昔替尼等口服JAK抑制剂。泽普昔替尼未来若顺利获批，仍需面对较为充分的市场竞争，其疗效、安全性及长期用药表现将成为影响市场竞争力的重要因素。从首次合作到权益扩容，先声药业与凌科药业进一步深化泽普昔替尼的商业化合作。随着特应性皮炎适应症进入上市申请审评阶段，这款国产口服JAK1抑制剂的后续进展值得关注。参考来源：[1] Journavx, notably, was dinged by one-time rebate accounting, so the “softer” quarter shouldn’t raise major concerns about the product, according to RBC Capital Markets analyst Brian Abrahams. In a note to clients, Abrahams wrote that the “solid” performance from Vertex’s cystic fibrosis drugs “underscores one of the steadiest, high-margin, and likely most durable core large biopharma franchises.” Vertex slightly upped its annual revenue guidance on Monday afternoon, to a range of $13.15 billion to $13.25 billion. Company shares, meanwhile, were down about 3% by mid-morning Tuesday. In his own note, David Risinger of Leerink Partners pointed out that Vertex’s earnings per share this quarter were 4% below consensus. The operating and financing costs associated with Crinetics — an endocrine drug developer that Vertex just purchased for $10 billion — also put pressure on near-term earnings. One of the bigger pieces of “good news,” according to Risinger and others, is that company leaders expressed confidence in their ability to launch Vertex’s first kidney product. But being marked as an important growth driver has also put a magnifying glass on the potential obstacles to pove’s commercial prospects. For example, a citizen’s petition filed in late October asked the FDA to, for safety reasons, require regular monitoring of antibody levels for patients taking the drug, as well as guidance for managing low levels. Two similar medicines are already available, too. Additionally, Vertex wants to provide pove as a highly concentrated, low volume shot delivered about once a month via an at-home autoinjector. Developing and scaling the manufacturing for that kind of product is often challenging. Still, Vertex executives affirmed their conviction. With the FDA’s decision deadline fast-approaching, “we are 100% ready” to sell the product and “are incredibly excited to bring pove to patients,” McKechnie said. The company “essentially gave bulls what they wanted to hear,” wrote Carter Gould, an analyst at Cantor Fitzgerald, in a note to clients. “Given that this was arguably one of the last opportunities to potentially reset expectations around approval or the label ahead of the [decision deadline], management's repeated expressions of confidence should be viewed as strongly encouraging,” Gould added. Earlier this year, when Vertex reported key late-stage data for pove, Gould described the results as “the first major step” to unlocking a renal franchise that could exceed $10 billion in peak annual sales. Such a franchise would go “a long way toward differentiating Vertex’s growth profile [versus its] larger-cap peers.” Another core piece of that franchise is inaxaplin, which is in testing as a treatment for kidney disease caused by mutations in a gene called APOL1. Analysts noted that Vertex leadership sounded confident in an upcoming trial readout for inaxaplin — another “potentially major catalyst” for the company’s stock, according to Christopher Raymond of Raymond James. content: An article from Dive Brief Genmab soars to record highs after cancer drug succeeds in key trial The latest data adds to a streak of readouts that could position the company to surpass $10 billion in total annual revenue in the years ahead, according to analysts. Published Oct. 29, 2026 Delilah Alvarado Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Courtesy of Genmab A/S Dive Brief: An experimental drug that Genmab gained in an $8 billion buyout succeeded in a late-stage trial in a form of head and neck cancer, sending shares of the Danish drugmaker soaring to an all-time high. At an early analysis, a combination of Genmab’s drug petosemtamab and the immunotherapy Keytruda, cut the risk of death by half compared to Keytruda alone when used as a first-line treatment in people whose head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is positive for the protein PD-L1. The regimen met dual main objectives on response rates and survival. The latest finding represents the third consecutive positive late-stage readout in a few weeks for Genmab, providing an important boost ahead of the patent expiry for the multiple myeloma drug Darzalex. The company will share detailed results with global regulatory authorities and present them at a future medical meeting. Though Johnson & Johnson owns commercial rights to Darzalex, Genmab derives royalties that heavily contributed to the roughly $3.7 billion in revenue the company booked in 2025. Genmab inherited petosemtamab when it acquired the Dutch biotechnology company Merus last year. The drug — a bispecific antibody targeting the proteins EGFR and LGR5 — had already produced positive results in a Phase 2 trial. Genmab predicted the antibody could become a blockbuster by 2029, should those results be replicated in a late-stage study. Ahead of those findings, Genmab scored two other wins that have lifted its revenue potential. Earlier this month, the company and partner AbbVie announced the blood cancer drug Epkinly succeeded in a Phase 3 trial in frontline lymphoma. Wall Street analysts claimed the results have positioned Epkinly to become a new treatment standard in people with newly diagnosed, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The company continued its streak last week when an antibody-drug conjugate dubbed rinatabart sesutecan hit its goal in a late-stage study in ovarian cancer. Genmab picked up that therapy in a 2024 buyout of startup ProfoundBio. Wednesday’s result positions petosemtamab to become part of a new treatment standard in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, wrote TD Cowen analyst Yaron Werber. The findings should support a “broad” label enabling access regardless of whether patients’ tumors are driven by HPV infections, he wrote. The trio of successes show Genmab has “delivered on the late-stage catalysts that define the company’s longer-term growth story,” wrote William Blair analyst Matt Phipps, in a Thursday client note. The company is now on the path to surpassing $10 billion in annual revenue, with pending launches that can “more than offset the impending loss of Darzalex royalties,” Phipps added. Petosemtamab is being tested in multiple other Phase 3 trials, among them studies in second- and third-line recurrent head and neck cancer, and a trial in colorectal cancer. FXIa，特异性阻断由中性粒细胞胞外诱捕网（NETs）、多聚磷酸盐等内源性激活物驱动的病理性血栓形成，同时保留生理性止血功能，有望在发挥抗栓作用的同时降低出血风险。2026年10月国内获批上市的新药截图来源：摩熵咨询《2026年10月全球在研新药月报》二、全球获孤儿药/突破性/快速通道资格认定品种盘点10月29日，和黄医药宣布索乐匹尼布获美国FDA授予孤儿药资格，用于治疗原发免疫性血小板减少症。免疫性血小板减少症是一种导致出血风险增加的自身免疫疾病。索乐匹尼布是一种新型、高选择性的口服脾酪氨酸激酶 (Syk) 抑制剂。10月全球孤儿药/突破性/快速通道资格认定品种一览表（部分）截图来源：摩熵咨询《2026年10月全球在研新药月报》三、全球在研创新药积极/失败临床结果TOP2010月11日，阿斯利康罕见病业务部门Alexion公布了酶替代疗法 efzimfotase alfa（ALXN1850）的全球III期HICKORY临床试验结果。在既往未接受过Strensiq（asfotase alfa）治疗的低磷酸酯酶症（HPP）青少年和成年患者（≥12岁）中展开。在第25周时，与安慰剂组相比，efzimfotase alfa在主要终点“六分钟步行试验”（6MWT）中显示出数值上的改善，最小二乘（LS）均值差为17.05米（p=0.1675），因成年发病型HPP安慰剂组表现优于预期而未达到统计学显著性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库10月12日，Syndax Pharmaceuticals宣布，axatilimab治疗特发性肺纤维化（IPF）的MAXPIRe 2期临床试验未达到主要终点，即用力肺活量（FVC）年下降率。试验中观察到的安全性与耐受性特征与此前研究一致，未发现新的安全信号。基于该试验结果，Syndax计划停止axatilimab在IPF领域的进一步开发，但该结果不会影响axatilimab在其他潜在适应症中的临床试验。Axatilimab是一款靶向集落刺激因子-1受体（CSF-1R）的单克隆抗体，商品名为Niktimvo（axatilimab-csfr）。该药在2024年8月已获美国FDA批准，用于治疗体重至少40公斤、既往至少两种系统性治疗失败的成年及儿童cGVHD患者。全球在研创新药积极/失败临床结果TOP20截图来源：摩熵咨询《2026年10月全球在研新药月报》四、全球创新药研发进展TOP2010月2日，礼来宣布，美国FDA已批准匹妥布替尼（Pirtobrutinib，100毫克和50毫克片剂）一项新增适应症上市，用于治疗既往未接受过治疗且无已知17p缺失的成人慢性淋巴细胞白血病或小淋巴细胞淋巴瘤 临床试验的主要分析结果。匹妥布替尼是一种高选择性、非共价BTK抑制剂，也是首个且目前唯一获批上市的非共价BTK抑制剂，可与野生型和C481突变型BTK结合，BTK是多种B细胞白血病和淋巴瘤中已验证的分子靶点。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此前，FDA已批准匹妥布替尼用于治疗多个适应症，包括复发或难治性套细胞淋巴瘤（MCL）成人患者（三线及以上）、既往接受过共价BTK抑制剂治疗的复发或难治性CLL/SLL成人患者。此外，9月28日NMPA官网显示，匹妥布替尼片的新适应症已在中国获批上市。全球创新药研发进展TOP20截图来源：摩熵咨询《2026年10月全球在研新药月报》五、全球医药企业热门BD交易事件10月1日，赛诺菲（Sanofi）与再生元今日联合宣布，双方扩大长期全球抗体研发合作，将4款由再生元发现的新一代长效免疫学抗体纳入合作，包括临床阶段长效白细胞介素-13（IL-13）单克隆抗体REGN20423、长效白细胞介素-4（IL-4）/IL-13双特异性抗体，以及另外两款分别靶向IL-4和白细胞介素-4受体α（IL-4Rα）的临床前长效抗体。根据协议，再生元将获得赛诺菲支付的10亿美元首付款，并有资格获得最高70亿美元的开发、监管和商业化里程碑付款。双方将平均分担新增项目的开发和商业化成本。再生元将牵头研发活动，赛诺菲负责全球商业化。根据此次协议，再生元还获得一项选择权，可在赛诺菲的lunsekimig完成治疗慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）的相关3期研究后，将其纳入双方合作。10月更多企业热门BD交易事件信息详见下表：以上内容均来自摩熵咨询｛ He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. After months of anticipation, the Food and Drug Administration gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories to make a generic version of a groundbreaking HIV prevention medicine, a key step in widening access for dozens of low- and middle-income countries. The company, one of the world’s largest generic drugmakers, plans to start shipping the medicine next month as part of an effort propelled, in part, by several global health organizations to ensure the drug becomes available in lower-income countries as quickly as possible. The annual cost per person will be $40, comparable to daily tablets.Advertisement Known as lenacapavir, the injectable drug is widely seen as a game-changing tool for eradicating HIV because it offers virtually complete protection against contracting the virus with just one administration every six months. The brand-name version, which is known as Yetzugo in the U.S., is marketed by Gilead Sciences and was approved by the FDA last year. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? title: 石药集团牵手康方生物：B7-H3 ADC SYS6043联合PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西，国内联合疗法临床正式启动
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 石药集团牵手康方生物：B7-H3 ADC SYS6043联合PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西，国内联合疗法临床正式启动 石药集团牵手康方生物：B7-H3 ADC SYS6043联合PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西，国内联合疗法临床正式启动 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 2026/11/03 2838 CD276 PD-1 VEGF 中山康方生物医药有限公司 石药集团有限公司 11月2日，石药集团与康方生物宣布达成临床合作，双方将围绕石药自主研发的B7-H3 ADC（SYS6043）与康方PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西注射液开展联合开发，合作区域为中国大陆，相关临床试验成果由双方共同所有。图源：石药集团企业官微ADC与免疫疗法联合开发并不新鲜，但此次合作有一个值得关注的细节：石药选择的不是传统PD-1单抗，而是同时靶向PD-1和VEGF的双抗依沃西。这也释放出一个信号：随着ADC联合疗法不断推进，PD-1/VEGF双抗正成为创新药企业探索ADC联合治疗的新选择。一、B7-H3 ADC联手PD-1/VEGF双抗SYS6043由石药巨石生物自主研发，是一款靶向B7-H3的新一代ADC，采用拓扑异构酶I抑制剂作为载荷，DAR约为6，采用Fcγ受体效应沉默设计以降低脱靶毒性，具有可裂解连接子和旁观者效应。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库临床数据方面，2026年ESMO公布的乳腺癌队列数据显示，在139例患者中，TNBC、HR+/HER2-及HER2+亚组的确认客观缓解率（ORR）分别达到75.0%、53.7%和69.6%；3级及以上治疗期间不良事件发生率为28.8%，间质性肺病发生率为1.4%。此外，2026年ASCO公布的全瘤种I/II期研究数据显示，533例可评估患者整体ORR为41.8%，其中肺癌和乳腺癌亚组ORR分别为46.3%和56.8%。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次合作的另一款药——依沃西，是康方生物自主研发的PD-1/VEGF双特异性抗体，目前已获批3项适应症。在临床研究中，依沃西已展现出一定的头对头竞争优势。例如，HARMONi-6研究中，依沃西联合化疗一线治疗鳞状非小细胞肺癌，中位总生存期（mOS）达到27.9个月，对照组为23.7个月；HARMONi-2研究中，依沃西单药一线治疗PD-L1阳性非小细胞肺癌，mOS达到30.8个月，对照组为22.6个月。值得注意的是，此次石药选择依沃西作为SYS6043的联合开发搭档，而非简单采用传统PD-1单抗，也让这笔合作有了更多值得关注的地方。二、ADC联合疗法，竞争逻辑正在变化为什么PD-1/VEGF双抗开始受到ADC研发企业关注？传统PD-1抑制剂主要通过解除T细胞的免疫抑制状态发挥作用，而VEGF除了促进肿瘤血管生成，还参与肿瘤免疫微环境的调节。因此，PD-1/VEGF双抗能够同时作用于免疫检查点和VEGF通路，有望改善肿瘤免疫微环境，为ADC联合治疗提供新的协同思路。简单来说，ADC负责靶向递送细胞毒载荷、杀伤肿瘤细胞，VEGF阻断有望改善免疫抑制微环境，PD-1阻断则帮助恢复T细胞抗肿瘤活性。三种作用机制存在潜在互补性。这一方向已经吸引多家药企布局。康方生物此前披露，阿斯利康、GSK、辉瑞、吉利德等跨国药企，以及国内多家ADC企业，均已开展核心ADC产品与依沃西的联合疗法探索。此外，BNT324/DB-1311联合PD-L1/VEGF双抗Pumitamig，以及科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC SKB500联合自研PD-1/VEGF双抗SKB118，也在推进相关联合治疗探索。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库这意味着，ADC与PD-1/VEGF双抗的联合开发正在成为值得关注的研发方向。对于康方生物而言，依沃西与多家ADC企业建立合作，有望进一步拓展其联合治疗布局，积累不同靶点、不同瘤种的临床数据。对于石药集团而言，此次合作则为SYS6043增加了一种新的联合治疗开发路径。从单一药物研发到联合治疗探索，ADC赛道的竞争正在延伸至联合搭档的选择。依沃西能否凭借已有临床数据和不断扩大的合作网络，形成差异化竞争优势，仍有待后续临床研究验证。 title: STAT Plus: Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent
content: STAT PlusBiotech Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent Biotech aspires to turn pill into a therapy for multiple immunology and inflammatory disorders Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 2, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. Over the past decade, Sanofi and Regeneron’s Dupixent has become the top-selling drug in immunology, bringing in tens of billions in revenue while transforming outcomes for the 1.4 million patients currently on the therapy for conditions including eczema, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. But investors and doctors are intensely following an experimental therapy positioned to rival the pharma blockbuster, with results from a key study fast approaching. Massachusetts biotech Kymera Therapeutics plans to announce data from a mid-stage clinical trial of its lead asset, KT-621, in eczema before the end of the year. Market analysts for the investment bank Jefferies, using common shorthand for immunology and inflammatory disorders, have called the upcoming results “one of the most impactful I&I readouts this year.” Advertisement Success (or failure) could have major consequences for Kymera, its growing list of competitors, and the millions of people who live with eczema in the United States. The results could also bolster or dampen the biotech’s aspirations to treat a broader class of immunological diseases with its drug, including chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Analysts forecast that the drug’s sales could reach nearly $4 billion by 2035, including more than $3 billion in eczema revenue, according to Visible Alpha. content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 3, 2026 Karyopharm Enters Chapter 11 in Planned Merger With Ayrmid Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Karyopharm filed for Chapter 11 under a plan to merge with Ayrmid, with competing bids allowed and closing targeted for the first quarter of 2027. Advertisement Karyopharm Therapeutics, the maker of the multiple myeloma treatment Xpovio (selinexor), filed for Chapter 11 protection on Nov. 2 under a restructuring support agreement that provides for a merger with Ayrmid, the parent company of Gamida Cell.1 The plan would convert roughly $276 million of funded debt into a majority stake in the combined company and cancel existing common and preferred shares without a distribution.2The company will seek court approval of bidding procedures that allow other parties to submit competing offers, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027.1 “Following a comprehensive review of available alternatives, we believe this process provides a clear framework to pursue a value maximizing transaction for our stakeholders while continuing our important work of advancing therapies for patients with multiple myeloma and myelofibrosis,” said Richard Paulson, president and CEO of Karyopharm.1Key FactsDeal: Ayrmid merger through Chapter 11 planLead bidder: Ayrmid; rival bids allowedDebtor-in-possession financing: up to $55MDebt holders to receive 55% of combined companyExisting shareholders: no distributionProduct: Xpovio (selinexor), exportin 1 inhibitorTarget close: first quarter of 2027“We see considerable potential in Karyopharm’s marketed products, development pipeline and experienced team, and believe that, together, we can build a broader, stronger commercial-stage hematology business with meaningful opportunities for future growth.” — Dr. Joe Wiley, chairman and chief executive officer of AyrmidWhat are the proposed merger terms?Under the plan described in Karyopharm’s disclosure statement, which the court has not yet approved, creditors holding the roughly $276 million of funded debt would receive 55% of the combined company’s common stock, along with contingent value rights tied to future Xpovio sales in myelofibrosis.2 Ayrmid’s existing equity holders would receive the remaining 45% and contingent equity tied to future revenue from its product Omisirge.2 The combined company would emerge with no more than $135 million of funded debt, a reduction of about $141 million, and Karyopharm’s common stock is expected to be delisted from Nasdaq.2Karyopharm has secured commitments for up to $55 million in debtor-in-possession financing from existing secured lenders, which, with cash from operations, is expected to support the business during the case once the court approves it.1 The company says it expects ordinary operations and partnerships to continue without disruption.1 The market test remains open: if a rival bid meets conditions that include at least $335 million in net proceeds at closing, the company may pursue a sale instead of the merger.2Why did Karyopharm file for Chapter 11?The disclosure statement attributes the filing to sustained operating losses and a reliance on capital markets that depended on clinical progress.2 When two phase 3 readouts in 2026 fell short of expectations and liquidity tightened, secured creditors agreed to payment deferrals and forbearances.2 A formal sale process launched in July 2026 drew multiple proposals, none of which was actionable before the company exhausted its liquidity, according to the filing.2 Ayrmid’s proposal emerged from that process.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof stated priority. In the phase 3 SENTRY trial of 353 patients, 50% of those given selinexor plus ruxolitinib reached a spleen volume reduction of at least 35% at week 24, versus 28% with ruxolitinib alone, but the groups did not differ significantly on the symptom-score co-primary endpoint, according to company-reported topline results.4 Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 70% of patients on the combination and 50% on ruxolitinib alone.4 Karyopharm submitted a supplemental new drug application seeking accelerated approval on Aug. 31, 2026.2How does the merger fit hematology commercial strategy?Ayrmid markets two FDA-approved products in the United States: Omisirge (omidubicel-onlv), a cell therapy for certain hematologic malignancies and severe aplastic anemia, and Aphexda (motixafortide), which mobilizes hematopoietic stem cells in adults with multiple myeloma.1 Multiple myeloma is the point at which the two companies’ marketed products overlap. “We see a strong strategic fit between Ayrmid and Karyopharm, with complementary portfolios, established commercial capabilities and a shared commitment to addressing significant unmet needs in hematology,” said Dr. Joe Wiley, chairman and chief executive officer of Ayrmid.1What risks and open questions remain?The plan still requires court confirmation. Holders of all claims entitled to vote have agreed to support it, according to the filing, so uncertainty centers on court approval, rival bids and regulatory reviews.2 Creditor voting closes Nov. 30, and the company has asked for a hearing on Jan. 11, 2027.2 Antitrust and foreign investment reviews are under evaluation, while FDA approval of the transaction itself is not expected to be required.2Projections for the combined company will be filed later with a plan supplement, so the commercial case remains unquantified.2 No FDA decision on the myelofibrosis application is reported in the sources reviewed, and SENTRY’s mixed result leaves that program’s regulatory outcome unsettled.2SourcesKaryopharm Therapeutics Inc. announces planned merger with Ayrmid Ltd. to strengthen company for the future. content: An article from News roundup UniQure gets an FDA decision date; Teva scraps brain drug study The FDA appears likely to hold an advisory committee for UniQure’s closely watched Huntington’s disease gene therapy. Elsewhere, a biotech’s share price was cut in half following a regulatory setback. Published Nov. 3, 2026 By BioPharma Dive staff Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving UniQure and Bridge Minds Biosciences, as well as updates from Specific Biologics, Teva Pharmaceuticals and CinRx Pharma that you may have missed. Following a high-profile back and forth with UniQure, the Food and Drug Administration has agreed to review an approval application for the company’s Huntington’s disease gene therapy. UniQure said Monday the agency is doing a faster-than-usual review and should have a verdict by May 1. The FDA is also tentatively planning to discuss the application in a meeting with external advisors, according to UniQure. Though company shares had fallen 7% by late Monday, Wall Street analysts generally viewed the update as positive for what could be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s. Joseph Thome, of TD Cowen, wrote in a note to clients that his team expects key doctors in the field to adopt the therapy. According to the medication’s developer, New York-based Bright Minds Biosciences, the primary reason the FDA gave for the partial hold was toxicity identified in mouse testing. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. Gilead is simultaneously building in ADCs, T-cell engagers for autoimmune disease, and now masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors — a deliberate multi-mechanism oncology buildout executed across a single year.Bausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat happened at Bausch + Lomb?Bausch + Lomb announced that Brent Saunders departed as CEO by mutual agreement, with Thomas J. Appio named interim CEO effective immediately. Appio, who will retain his role as CEO of parent company Bausch Health, steps into the position just weeks before the company reports third-quarter results and updates its full-year guidance on October 28.What does the company expect for 2026?Simultaneously with the leadership announcement, both Bausch + Lomb and Bausch Health said they expect to raise their full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance based on preliminary third-quarter results, citing strong business performance and anticipated momentum through year-end.What was Saunders building?Saunders returned to Bausch + Lomb in March 2023 — his second stint as CEO — and spent three years stabilizing the company’s supply chain, accelerating commercial execution, and rebuilding its R&D pipeline. 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 16小时前 962 BTK ELANE 山东新时代药业有限公司 急性呼吸窘迫综合征 肺损伤 11月4日，CDE官网显示，重庆华邦制药再次提交的3类仿制药注射用西维来司他钠上市申请获得受理。图源：CDE官网此前，公司于2026年6月3日首次提交上市申请，但未获批准。时隔一个月再次申报，这一上市6年来长期由上海汇伦独家供应、年销售额达数亿元的品种，正迎来新的竞争者。一、5亿级市场，5家药企扎堆申报注射用西维来司他钠主要用于改善伴有全身性炎症反应综合征（SIRS）的急性肺损伤（ALI）或急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ARDS）患者，是全球唯一获批用于治疗SIRS相关ALI/ARDS的靶向药物。该药由日本小野制药研发，于2002年4月11日在日本获批上市，属于中性粒细胞弹性蛋白酶（NE）竞争性抑制剂，可通过抑制NE活性发挥治疗作用。目前，原研产品尚未在国内上市，上海汇伦是国内首家获批企业。据摩熵医药数据库显示，2025年注射用西维来司他钠全终端市场销售额超过5亿元，2026年上半年销售额达到3.46亿元，同比增长32.78%。 2014年，上海汇伦曾提交该品种3.1类新药上市申请，但受2015年药物临床试验数据自查影响，最终主动撤回。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库2020年，新冠疫情期间，西维来司他钠临床需求增加，上海汇伦再次提交上市申请，并在应急审评背景下仅用27天便获批。这一快速获批背后，是上海汇伦此前多年的研发积累。据摩熵医药数据库显示，在提交上市申请前，公司已开展2次药代动力学试验、1次安全性和有效性试验，并于2018年补充开展2次药代动力学试验。该品种最初以附条件批准方式获批，此后经多项上市后研究，目前已转为常规批准。上市后，西维来司他钠（商品名：希为纳）一度成为上海汇伦的核心收入来源。2026年4月，上海汇伦医药向港交所递交招股书。招股书显示，2023年希为纳销售收入达到7.45亿元，占公司总营收的75.7%；2024年降至4.24亿元，2025年进一步降至3.70亿元，收入占比也降至54.0%。从国内首家获批到长期独家供应，希为纳曾为上海汇伦贡献了重要收入。如今，随着山东新时代药业、重庆华邦制药等5家企业相继申报上市，这款独家品种正逐步迎来竞争者。未来，随着仿制药审评进程推进，注射用西维来司他钠的市场竞争格局或将发生变化。参考来源：[1] content: An article from Dive Brief // Gene editing FDA unveils guidance for ‘plug and play’ gene therapies The plan builds on recent FDA moves to speed “personalized” treatments by offering an approval framework for therapies benefiting different subsets of patients with the same disease. Win McNamee / Staff via Getty Images Dive Brief: The Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday took another step toward expanding access to treatments for rare diseases, announcing a new proposal for personalized gene therapies. In the latest draft guidance, regulators focused on treatments designed to correct different mutations in the same disease-causing gene. Often, the individual mutations are so rare that traditional clinical trials are impractical or even impossible. Under the plan, a drugmaker could win approval for a specific personalized gene therapy targeting one mutation using more of a traditional approach, then later win clearance for different mutations with laboratory data instead of a whole new clinical study. But most people with rare diseases face the stark fact that developing individual treatments requiring clinical studies just isn’t profitable for drugmakers. With the latest plan, the FDA is hoping to change the economic calculus, allowing what TD Cowen analyst Joseph Thome called a “plug and play” optionality. If enacted, this draft guidance could be especially relevant for products under development by gene editing specialist Prime Medicine, Thome wrote in a note to clients. Prime shares jumped 15% early Wednesday. Beam Therapeutics CEO John Evans says the idea would help his company too. “All of this is completely supported by the science of base editing,” Evans wrote in a series of posts on the social media platform X, referring to Beam’s core drug development technology. “But it’s still exhilarating to see the FDA crafting such a forward-looking approach.” Beam’s shares rose 8%. The idea is part of a larger effort by the FDA to encourage drugmakers to develop treatments for rare diseases. The agency is holding a meeting Wednesday afternoon on its White Oak campus to discuss its “Rare Disease Framework Initiative,” which aims to set standards for individual conditions rather than the standard one-size-fits-all approach. Agency officials also attended a rare disease summit in Washington this week. “Senior policymakers are clearly supportive of rare disease,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Luca Issi wrote in a note to clients about the summit. Issi sees a contrast with the “darker days” when former FDA officials Marty Makary and Vinay Prasad left drugmakers frustrated and confused by a series of hard-line stances on therapies even as they unveiled proposals designed to help speed products to market. As part of the administration’s rare disease efforts, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services is also looking to broaden a program that gives Medicaid patients access to cell and gene therapies. Initially, the focus was on sickle cell disease. A big question for developers of gene-editing medicines has been whether one-time prices would become a “roadblock,” Beam’s Evans wrote on X. “Or would payers work to ensure access for patients and capture the long-term benefits of eliminating lifelong medical expenses and chronic treatments?” The CMS plan to expand its access program is “great news,” he said. 创新药与医疗器械虽分属不同产品体系，但均高度依赖外部研发服务支持产品开发、注册申报和上市转化。与此同时，两类产品在研发逻辑、监管路径、证据要求和项目组织方式上存在明显差异，这也决定了两类CRO不能简单沿用同一商业模式分析框架。基于此，摩熵咨询发布的医药洞察简报《创新药CRO与医疗器械CRO商业模式差异分析》系统比较了两类CRO在产品属性、服务链条、盈利模式、客户结构、能力壁垒、服务单元价值和企业筛选口径等方面的差异，以厘清二者在服务逻辑、价值创造方式和竞争壁垒上的实质区别。一、行业背景：两类CRO同源不同路，底层产品属性决定商业模式创新药、医疗器械均大量借助外部CRO机构完成研发验证、合规申报与上市转化，但二者产品底层逻辑完全不同，直接造成创新药CRO商业模式与医疗器械CRO商业模式出现系统性分化。创新药分子靶点、药理毒理评价、临床试验体系具备较强标准化特征，研发周期普遍10年以上，风险集中在I-III期关键临床阶段，监管体系以GLP、GCP、CTD资料体系为核心，核心评判指标是药物的安全性、有效性、统计学终点结果。医疗器械品类极其繁杂，覆盖有源设备、无源植入耗材、IVD、AI医疗软件，跨机械、电子、材料、生物多学科；研发风险前置在产品分类界定、检验路径、临床评价方案设计，监管围绕产品风险等级划分，重点考核产品性能、使用安全性、临床适用场景匹配度，不同品类之间经验很难直接复用。核心结论：产品属性是根源。创新药CRO商业模式更容易做标准化、规模化大项目；医疗器械CRO商业模式更强调注册策略前置介入、细分赛道Know-how与定制化项目交付。产品属性决定二者商业模式差异图源：摩熵咨询《创新药CRO与医疗器械CRO商业模式差异分析》二、全流程服务链条对比：创新药覆盖全生命周期，器械聚焦注册转化2.1 创新药CRO完整服务链条创新药CRO商业模式覆盖从药物发现一直到上市后药物警戒的完整全生命周期，临床开发与数据统计是价值高地。药物发现阶段：靶点验证、化合物筛选、DEL库、先导化合物发现、早期成药性评估；临床前研究：药理药效、PK/PD、GLP毒理安全性评价、CMC制剂工艺开发，支撑IND申报；临床CRO阶段：I/II/III/IV期多中心临床试验、生物样本分析、统计分析、医学写作；注册及上市后：注册申报、药物警戒、RWE真实世界研究、上市后安全性研究。特点：项目周期普遍10年+，投入规模大，可承接一站式一体化全流程外包，临床阶段是价值核心。2.2 医疗器械CRO完整服务链条医疗器械CRO商业模式并不深度介入产品早期硬件/软件原型开发，核心聚焦合规验证、注册路径规划、临床评价、质量体系搭建、上市后合规跟踪，最终目标是推动产品完成注册获批上市。临床前合规验证：生物相容性、老化灭菌包装、电气安全EMC、动物性能验证；注册策略规划：产品分类界定、证据缺口分析、风险评估、注册路径设计；临床服务：同品种比对（二类器械主流）、临床试验（三类高风险器械）、多中心项目管理；质量体系与上市后：ISO13485体系搭建、设计开发文档、注册申报、不良事件监测跟踪。特点：项目周期更短，以分阶段小项目为主；注册路径、临床评价、质量体系构建是服务核心，重点解决注册不确定性。三、盈利模式与收入结构差异3.1 创新药CRO盈利特征收费模式同时存在FTE人天计费、项目打包FFS、阶段里程碑三类模式；大型全球多中心临床项目合同金额高，订单向头部大客户集中上海证券报。成本结构：重资产属性明显，投入集中于GLP安评实验室、动物平台、临床运营团队、统计数据系统；毛利弹性：大分子、ADC、全球多中心临床、生物统计等复杂业务具备高溢价；但项目毛利会受客户管线失败、项目暂停的冲击；收入稳定性：依赖头部药企长期框架协议带来稳定现金流，但也会面临管线收缩、入组不及预期、项目终止带来的收入波动。概括创新药CRO商业模式：依靠大客户、长周期框架、大项目，规模效应突出，高附加值临床业务拉动毛利。3.2 医疗器械CRO盈利特征收费模式以固定项目打包、分阶段收费为主，里程碑、权益分成模式非常少见；整体呈现“小单、多项目”特征。成本结构：偏向轻资产，主要成本是法规专家、临床资源协调、检验对接、文档撰写人力；毛利弹性：创新器械临床评价、MDR/FDA海外注册咨询、AI器械RWE真实世界服务溢价高；普通注册代理、基础文档整理同质化严重，价格竞争激烈；收入稳定性：客户高度分散，单个项目金额低，客户跨品类切换服务商门槛不高；但项目周转快、回款节奏相对灵活。概括医疗器械CRO商业模式：收入来自大量分散项目，核心竞争力是细分赛道经验、注册转化效率、项目周转能力。盈利模式差异驱动二者收入结构分化图源：摩熵咨询《创新药CRO与医疗器械CRO商业模式差异分析》四、客户结构、订单特征与增长路径4.1 创新药CRO客户与订单客户群体以跨国药企MNC、国内大型药企、Biotech为主，客户集中度相对更高。订单特征：长周期、分阶段打包、全流程一体化项目占比高；同一个药物管线可以持续延展多个研发阶段，客户黏性较强；业务协同：可以和CDMO、统计、药物警戒、注册申报形成一体化协同；头部客户一般签署年度框架，预算规模大。4.2 医疗器械CRO客户与订单客户以中小器械厂商、初创器械企业、医院成果转化项目为主，客户极度分散，几乎没有超级大客户。订单特征：大多为单次注册、临床评价、质量体系辅导等节点型项目；单项目预算有限，客户更换服务商的门槛较低，复购高度依赖注册效率与细分项目案例；业务协同：主要和检测机构、质量体系咨询、上市后监测、真实世界证据服务做组合交付。增长抓手对比：创新药CRO商业模式靠大客户深挖、管线延续复购；医疗器械CRO商业模式靠细分赛道口碑、项目周转效率、品类拓展。客户结构与订单特征决定两类CRO增长路径差异图源：摩熵咨询《创新药CRO与医疗器械CRO商业模式差异分析》订单逻辑差异：（1）客户集中度——创新药CRO客户更集中，医疗器械CRO客户更分散。（2）合作周期——创新药偏长周期与管线延展，器械偏项目制与节点交付。（3）增长抓手——创新药依赖大客户与复购，器械依赖注册效率与细分赛道能力。五、核心能力壁垒与企业扩张逻辑5.1 创新药CRO：重资产平台化扩张逻辑创新药CRO商业模式的核心壁垒来源于标准化平台能力，适合规模化复制扩张：GLP/安评实验平台：自有动物实验室、标准化安全性评价体系，构成硬门槛；全球申报能力：多国家法规沟通、国际多中心项目执行经验；临床网络与统计能力：医院中心资源、数据管理、生物统计、医学写作能力；扩张路径：依托重资产实验室、标准化SOP、全球临床网络，实现跨地区复制，走向平台型CRO/CRDMO。5.2 医疗器械CRO：细分赛道专精化逻辑医疗器械CRO商业模式壁垒不在于大型实验室，而在于细分品类Know how、法规判断力、临床场景资源，很难简单复制到其他器械品类：法规分类判断：产品风险等级、注册单元划分、临床评价路径预判，直接决定项目周期成败；产品工程理解：需要理解机械、电子、软件、材料交叉技术特征；科室与KOL资源：对应不同器械的临床使用场景、术者资源；质量体系能力：ISO13485、设计开发文档、上市后全流程合规；扩张路径：依靠垂直品类项目积累，走专科化、赛道化扩张，而不是简单平台复制。六、服务单元价值分层：资源配置的差异6.1 创新药CRO服务价值地图前沿布局服务（高壁垒，兑现周期长）：AI药物发现、复杂递送系统评价、海外新兴临床、新靶点验证；高价值核心服务（高订单、高技术壁垒）：大分子/ADC临床、全球多中心试验、复杂适应症临床、统计医学写作；现金流支撑服务（需求稳定）：常规安评、BE试验、数据管理、小分子筛选；低效收缩服务（同质化）：低附加值文档、简单筛选。资源配置策略：现金流业务维持运营，高价值核心业务拉动增长，前沿业务储备未来管线。6.2 医疗器械CRO服务价值地图前沿探索服务（新规则驱动）：MDR/FDA咨询、AI医疗器械、数字疗法RWE评价；高价值突破服务（溢价能力强）：创新器械临床、手术机器人、高端影像设备临床评价；现金流支撑服务（需求稳定）：二类器械同品种对比、常规三类注册、基础临床评价、质量体系辅导；低效收缩服务（价格内卷）：基础代办检测、低端耗材简单注册、纯文档整理跑腿业务。资源配置策略：基础注册项目维持基本盘，高价值创新器械服务打造溢价，前沿赛道跟踪新机会；减少低附加值跑腿类业务投入。七、企业筛选评价评分卡：两类CRO不能用同一套标准很多投资、产业评估会混淆两类外包服务商，实际上创新药CRO商业模式与医疗器械CRO商业模式评价维度差异显著。企业筛选评分卡：两类CRO应采用差异化评价口径图源：摩熵咨询《创新药CRO与医疗器械CRO商业模式差异分析》筛选要点：创新药CRO重点看大项目承接、临床网络、统计质量、全球申报、平台协同；医疗器械CRO重点看注册路径预判、细分赛道案例、临床评价组织、多服务组合交付。八、行业未来发展趋势8.1 创新药CRO发展趋势业务从单纯临床执行向一体化临床开发延伸；强化全球多中心、RWE真实世界、生物统计能力；业务向大分子、ADC、小核酸、细胞治疗等高复杂度前沿疗法升级；数字化项目管理、AI辅助方案设计、中心筛选逐步成为基础能力；价值锚点：研发执行效率、数据质量、全球管线协同能力。8.2 医疗器械CRO发展趋势服务从单点注册咨询，向前端检测、临床评价、质量体系、上市后全链条延伸；高端影像、手术机器人、AI医疗软件带动专业化细分服务需求爆发；真实世界证据RWE成为创新器械注册的重要证据来源；MDR、IVDR、FDA新法规倒逼服务商提升海外合规能力；价值锚点：注册路径确定性、临床场景验证、产品注册转化成功率。8.3 行业共同趋势数字化项目管理、电子数据系统EDC逐步普及；AI辅助方案设计、受试者/中心筛选、真实世界数据分析提升项目效率；从单一项目执行，转向组合式、打包式整体解决方案输出。最终判断：创新药CRO的核心价值在于提升研发效率、保障数据质量，并支撑复杂管线推进。医疗器械CRO的核心价值在于降低注册路径不确定性，提升产品验证与上市转化效率。两类CRO均在向高价值服务升级，但前者更偏平台化扩张，后者更偏细分赛道专精。九、总结与产业启示同为研发外包，创新药CRO商业模式与医疗器械CRO商业模式因底层产品属性不同，形成完全不一样的商业逻辑：创新药CRO依托标准化、重资产平台，走大客户、长周期、大项目的平台化扩张路线，核心价值是提升新药研发效率、保障临床数据质量，支撑复杂管线推进；医疗器械CRO依靠细分赛道专业积累，以大量中小定制项目为主，核心价值在于降低注册路径的不确定性，加速器械产品合规上市转化。对于企业选型：药企选CRO优先考察一体化平台、全球临床与统计交付实力；医疗器械企业优先考察对应细分品类项目案例、注册路径预判能力、临床场景资源，不要简单套用创新药CRO的评估标准。对于投资机构：两类CRO估值逻辑应分开看待，不能简单直接对标；创新药CRO看平台规模、框架订单、高复杂管线承接能力；医疗器械CRO重点看垂直赛道壁垒、项目周转效率、高端创新器械项目占比。展望未来，二者都向高附加值服务升级，但升级路径完全不同：创新药CRO向着全球化、复杂新疗法一体化服务演进；医疗器械CRO向着细分赛道专精、海外合规、真实世界证据方向深耕。认清二者商业模式差异，是项目立项、服务商选型、产业投资的重要前提。 WASHINGTON – Democrats’ landslide victory in the midterm elections may have significant implications for the upcoming negotiations over a key funding source for the Food and Drug Administration, in part by empowering a major critic of the program. The FDA collects user fees from pharmaceutical companies to fund the agency’s reviews of their medicines. The Prescription User Fee Drug Act must be renewed before the current law expires on Sept. 30. Otherwise, it could disrupt the FDA’s ability to approve medicines.Advertisement The power to shape that legislation will fall to senior Democrats, including Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who will likely lead the Senate’s health committee. Sanders is one of the few lawmakers who have opposed the core premise of the user fee structure.
